headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Default rules for when grain title passes
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 including subdivisions (1)-(3) and history note. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–4 (including subdivisions (1)–(3) of sub 3, definitions (1)–(27) and grain-dealer exclusions (17)(a)–(d) of sub 4) and history note (through 2012 S.B. 631); verified all source URLs and SHA-256 fingerprints. headings.title: Mandatory administrative, licensing, and bonding duties

headings.title: Original application filing fee under section 276.506

headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history/effective-date notes. headings.title: Corporate surety bond filing requirement and violation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/effective-date notes (L. 1980 H.B. 1627 § 6, A.L. 1986 H.B. 1578, A.L. 1997 H.B. 211; effective 4-02-97). headings.title: Bond beneficiaries, conditions, minimum price coverage, and note exclusion
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 including subdivisions (1)-(4) and history/effective-date notes. Designates Missouri as obligee (except under section 276.581) and the director as trustee for grain sellers, sets payment and faithful-performance conditions for in-state title transfers, covers minimum prices on valid minimum price contracts, and excludes signed promissory notes containing specified terms. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Continuous bond force and noncumulative liability cap
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history/effective-date notes. Makes surety bonds continuous from issue until cancelled regardless of license expiration, while prohibiting cumulative surety liability across successive license periods beyond the stated or endorsed bond amount. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Continuous bond maintenance and dealer cancellation restrictions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history/effective-date notes. Requires keeping the bond continuously in force while conducting business, makes lapse grounds for license revocation and chapter penalties, and prohibits dealer cancellation without prior written director approval and an approved substitute bond. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Same corporate surety required for dual chapter 411 licensees
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history/effective-date notes. Requires grain dealers also licensed under chapter 411 to use the same corporate surety for all chapter 411 and grain dealer bonds. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Payment demand, escrow, distribution hearings, appeals, and surety penalties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history/effective-date notes. Requires sureties upon written demand to pay the director or deposit into high-interest escrow within 10 days, governs court interpleader or chapter 536 administrative hearings and appeals, authorizes license withdrawal plus 25% penalty and interest for refusal, and directs refunds with interest if surety liability is lower or absent. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Ninety-day certified-mail notice for bond cancellation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history/effective-date notes. Requires every bond to prohibit cancellation by principal or surety without 90 days' prior certified-mail notice to the director in Jefferson City (with same-day certified copy to the principal if cancelled by the surety), preserves accrued liability during the 90 days, and keeps bonds in force if notice procedures are not followed. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: License suspension, revocation, and inspection after cancellation notice
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and history/effective-date notes. headings.title: Bank payment demand, escrow, distribution, weekly penalties, and refunds

headings.title: Minimum two-percent bond calculation formula
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. headings.title: Single cumulative bond for multiple licensed locations

headings.title: License sanctions for failing to maintain bond or statement

headings.title: Additional bond when purchases surpass initial estimates

headings.title: Discretionary license sanctions for statutory or rule violations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9 and history/effective-date notes. Authorizes the director to modify, suspend, cancel, revoke, or refuse to renew a license upon conviction or director determination of a violation of sections 276.401 to 276.581 or adopted rules. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Written order, certified-mail notice, appeal, and appeal bonds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 10 and history/effective-date notes. Requires a signed written order stating reasons sent by certified mail, allows chapter 536 appeal within 30 days of mailing, and requires posting both a costs bond and a jurisdictional bond covering all identified grain purchases and obligations through final state or federal review. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Revised title so the jurisdictional characterization is not over-applied to both the costs bond and the grain-obligations bond. (Prior draft: "Written order, certified-mail notice, appeal, and jurisdictional bonds".)

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–10 (including subdivisions (1)–(6) of sub 1 and (1)–(2) of sub 8) and history/effective-date notes (effective 4-22-86); verified all fingerprints. Confirmed retained archived range "276.401 to 276.581", 10-year manipulation bar, 15-day denial hearing request, section 276.421 renewal statement, nontransferability, mandatory vs. discretionary sanctions, and chapter 536 appeal with costs bond and jurisdictional grain-obligations bond. Revised sub 10 title to avoid over-applying "jurisdictional" to both bonds; retained subs 1–9.

headings.title: Public display of license and required materials
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including subdivisions (1)-(2) and history/effective-date notes (L. 1980 H.B. 1627 § 12, A.L. 1997 H.B. 211; effective 4-02-97). Requires each dealer to conspicuously display in unobstructed public view at each business location the original or certified copy of the license and any other director-required materials. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Issuance of certificates of license upon request
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history/effective-date notes. Directs the director, upon written request and fee payment, to issue certificates of license issuance or renewal under sections 276.401 to 276.582 in numbers based on demonstrated need. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Posting certificates at non-record locations and in vehicles
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history/effective-date notes. Requires posting a certificate of license at listed business locations where transaction records are not kept and carrying a certificate in each grain-transporting vehicle used for grain purchases and transport. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Display of license certificate upon demand and contents
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history/effective-date notes. Requires displaying the certificate of license upon demand and requires it to contain information deemed necessary by the director. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Director ownership and repossession of licenses and certificates
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history/effective-date notes. Declares all licenses and certificates of license the property of the director, subject to revocation, cancellation, or repossession under sections 276.401 to 276.582. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–5 (including subdivisions (1)–(2) of sub 1) and history/effective-date notes (effective 4-02-97); verified all fingerprints. Confirmed public display at business locations, issuance of license certificates upon request/fees under sections 276.401 to 276.582, posting at non-record locations and in grain-transporting vehicles, display on demand, and director ownership/repossession. All 5 drafted titles retained.

headings.title: General payment timing, price documentation, and director demands
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/effective-date notes (L. 1980 H.B. 1627 § 13, A.L. 1986 H.B. 1578, A.L. 1987 H.B. 751, A.L. 1997 H.B. 211; effective 4-02-97). Requires payment on delivery or demand unless a written purchase or valid deferred payment contract provides otherwise, mandates price documentation, authorizes verbal or written director payment requests (including certified/cashier check or cash), and permits license sanctions for nonpayment. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Class I dealer payment, settlement sheets, and contract deadline
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history/effective-date notes. Requires class I dealers to document prices and pay on demand or enter accounts onto a formal settlement sheet within 30 days of delivery, with payment due on demand or within 180 days, after which a written contract under subsections 8 and 11 must be executed. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Class II dealer payment, settlement sheets, and credit-contract ban
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history/effective-date notes. Requires class II dealers to document prices and pay on demand or enter accounts onto a formal settlement sheet within 30 days (payable on demand or within 180 days), and prohibits class II dealers from entering any credit sales contracts. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Class III through VI payment deadline and credit-contract ban
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history/effective-date notes. Requires class III, IV, V, and VI dealers to pay within 30 days of delivery or on demand (whichever occurs first) and bars them from entering any credit sales contracts. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Oral payment demands versus written demand for bond recovery
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history/effective-date notes. Preserves a seller's right to make oral payment demands while restricting recovery under the surety bond to written demand to the surety by the seller or by the department on the claimant's behalf. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Nonexclusivity of bond recovery and civil contract actions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history/effective-date notes. Provides that recovery on a surety bond is not a claimant's exclusive remedy and does not bar a civil action under the grain purchase contract. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Deferred price contracts, required disclosures, and bond exclusion
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history/effective-date notes. Excludes valid deferred price contracts from surety bond recovery, requires written dated disclosures of title transfer, lack of bond coverage, and common-claim status, and restricts use exclusively to class I dealers. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Deferred payment contracts, required disclosures, and twelve-month bond
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and history/effective-date notes. Authorizes only class I dealers to enter written dated deferred payment contracts containing required disclosures of title transfer, 12-month surety bond coverage from contract date, and common-claim status thereafter. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Bond coverage of recent deferred payment contracts upon revocation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9 and history/effective-date notes. Deems all deferred payment agreements executed within 12 months before a license revocation to be priced unpaid obligations as of revocation and covered by the dealer's bond. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Minimum price contracts, disclosures, and limited bond coverage
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 10 and history/effective-date notes. Authorizes only class I dealers to enter written dated minimum price contracts with required disclosures of title transfer, minimum price, gain calculation, 12-month bond coverage strictly for the minimum price, and no bond coverage for subsequent price gains. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Validity requirements for credit contracts and class II-VI ban
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 11 and history/effective-date notes. Makes deferred price, deferred payment, and minimum price contracts invalid unless containing all required statements and signed by both parties or authorized representatives, allows the director to require additional seller-protection information, and reiterates the ban for class II-VI dealers. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–11 and history/effective-date notes (effective 4-02-97); verified all fingerprints. Confirmed class I, class II, and class III–VI payment/settlement-sheet timelines and credit-contract bans, oral vs. written bond demand, nonexclusivity of bond recovery, class I-only deferred price (no bond), deferred payment (12-month bond, covered on revocation), and minimum price (12-month minimum-price bond only) contracts, and validity requirements. All 11 drafted titles retained.

headings.title: Current grain transaction records at principal business place
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/effective-date notes (L. 1980 H.B. 1627 § 15, A.L. 1997 H.B. 211; effective 4-02-97). Requires grain dealers to maintain current and complete records of all grain received, withdrawn, purchased, sold, and held at their principal place of business. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Required quantity, ticket, receipt, and direct-shipment records
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 including subdivisions (1)-(4) and history/effective-date notes. Requires keeping in a place of safety records of grain quantities by kind/class, duplicate issued receipts/tickets/bills of lading, cancelled originals, and a daily-updated register of direct farm-to-market shipments not evidenced by the dealer's own scale ticket. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Financial records supporting submitted regulatory information
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history/effective-date notes. Requires maintaining adequate financial records clearly reflecting current financial position and supporting information submitted to the director for licensing, auditing, inspection, or investigation. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Three-year record retention and examination access
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history/effective-date notes. Requires keeping all relevant books, records, and accounts available for director examination for at least three years after the close of the covered period during normal business hours or at noticed times. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Revised title because examinations may occur during normal business hours or at a prior-noticed time. (Prior draft: "Three-year record retention and business-hours examination".)

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–4 (including subdivisions (1)–(4) of sub 2) and history/effective-date notes (effective 4-02-97); verified all fingerprints. Confirmed principal-place transaction records, safety-kept quantity/ticket/receipt/daily direct-shipment records, financial records, and 3-year retention with examination during business hours or prior-noticed times. Revised sub 4 title to reflect both business-hours and prior-noticed examinations; retained subs 1–3.

headings.title: Inspection of dealer premises and business-hours records
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1980 H.B. 1627 § 17). Authorizes the director or section 276.476 auditors to inspect premises of licensees or persons reasonably believed to require licensing under sections 276.401 to 276.581 (archived range) at any time, and subjects dealer books and records to inspection during business hours. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Administration-based inspections from reports and information
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 1980 H.B. 1627 § 17). Permits the director to perform inspections necessary for orderly administration of sections 276.401 to 276.581 based on available reports and information. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Licensee cooperation and access to weighing and grading equipment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note (L. 1980 H.B. 1627 § 17). Requires licensees and their employees, agents, officers, partners, directors, and shareholders to cooperate and assist in inspections, including allowing reasonable use of weighing, sampling, and grading equipment. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Record production by out-of-state licensed dealers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note (L. 1980 H.B. 1627 § 17). Requires licensed dealers without a Missouri place of business to furnish all Missouri grain transaction records upon request at any time and place designated by the director. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Director authority to require seller-protection reports
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note (L. 1980 H.B. 1627 § 17). Permits requiring grain dealers to submit reports deemed necessary by the director to protect grain sellers under sections 276.401 to 276.581 and regulations. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Bills of lading or other transit grain documents
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note (L. 1980 H.B. 1627 § 17). Requires transporters of grain in transit to possess bills of lading or other covering documents and make them available for inspection upon request. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Revised title to include "other documents covering such grain in transit" alongside bills of lading. (Prior draft: "Bills of lading required for grain in transit".)

headings.title: Investigation of verified written complaints with reasonable basis
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history note (L. 1980 H.B. 1627 § 17). Directs the director to investigate verified written complaints alleging facts constituting violations or license sanction grounds, with a proviso exempting complaints lacking a reasonable basis. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Revised title to preserve the statutory proviso excusing investigation of complaints lacking a reasonable basis. (Prior draft: "Investigation of verified written complaints".)

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–7 and history note (L. 1980 H.B. 1627 § 17); verified all fingerprints. Confirmed retained archived range "276.401 to 276.581", section 276.476 auditor inspections, weighing/sampling/grading equipment access, out-of-state dealer production, seller-protection reports, transit bills of lading or other documents, and reasonable-basis proviso for verified complaints. Revised subs 6 and 7 titles for exact document scope and reasonable-basis qualification; retained subs 1–5.

headings.title: Restraining orders and injunctions against dealer violations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/effective-date notes (L. 1980 H.B. 1627 § 18, A.L. 1997 H.B. 211; effective 4-02-97). Authorizes the director (prosecuted by the attorney general or county prosecutor on request) to seek restraining orders or temporary/permanent injunctions enforcing sections 276.401 to 276.582 notwithstanding other legal remedies. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Injunctions against disposing of or removing grain
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history/effective-date notes. Authorizes the director (through the attorney general or county prosecutor) to seek restraining orders or injunctions barring a dealer from disposing of owned or held grain or barring anyone from removing grain in which the dealer or claimants have an interest. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Investigative and hearing powers, oaths, and subpoenas
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 including subdivisions (1)-(6) and history/effective-date notes. Grants the director six powers in investigations and hearings: examining persons under oath, examining dealer or warehouseman records, taking testimony/evidence, administering oaths, issuing subpoenas for witnesses and books, and serving subpoenas, petitions, or orders. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Circuit court orders and contempt enforcement for subpoenas
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history/effective-date notes. Authorizes any circuit court to order witness attendance and production of records subpoenaed by the director and compel compliance through contempt proceedings. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–4 (including subdivisions (1)–(6) of sub 3) and history/effective-date notes (effective 4-02-97); verified all fingerprints. Confirmed attorney general or county prosecutor injunctions against violations and grain disposal/removal under sections 276.401 to 276.582, six investigative/hearing powers, and circuit court subpoena enforcement by contempt. All 4 drafted titles retained.

headings.title: License modification, suspension, or revocation authority
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/effective-date notes (L. 1980 H.B. 1627 § 19, A.L. 1997 H.B. 211; effective 4-02-97). Authorizes the director, after a hearing or upon a verified complaint by any person, to modify, suspend, or revoke a license for violating or failing to comply with sections 276.401 to 276.582 or regulations. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Complaint filing, notice service, and hearing timeframe
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history/effective-date notes. Requires filing verified complaint grounds with the director and serving notice, complaint copy, and hearing order (set 5 to 30 days from notification) personally or by registered or certified mail. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Emergency temporary license suspension without prior hearing
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history/effective-date notes. Permits temporary suspension without hearing for up to 90 days upon finding immediate public-good need, reasonable cause of violation, and immediate danger of claimant loss, requiring a post-suspension hearing within five days. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Hearing presentation rights and continuances
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history/effective-date notes. Directs the director to hear charges at the noticed time and place, affords both licensee and complainant opportunity to present evidence and arguments in person or by counsel, and permits continuances. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Chapter 536 appeal of director decisions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history/effective-date notes. Permits any person aggrieved by the director's decision to appeal as provided in chapter 536. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: One-hundred-twenty-day bond claim deadline after revocation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history/effective-date notes. Requires filing claims against a former licensee and surety within 120 days after license revocation, defeating untimely claims for purposes of recovery under the grain dealer's bond. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Revised title to specify that untimely filing defeats recovery under the grain dealer's bond rather than all remedies. (Prior draft: "One-hundred-twenty-day claim deadline after license revocation".)

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–6 and history/effective-date notes (effective 4-02-97); verified all fingerprints. Confirmed verified-complaint notice (5–30 day hearing), emergency 90-day temporary suspension with 5-day post-suspension hearing, hearing rights/continuances, chapter 536 appeals, and 120-day post-revocation claim bar for bond recovery. Revised sub 6 title to specify bond claim deadline; retained subs 1–5.

headings.title: Terminating grain arrangements and notices upon revocation or expiration
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1980 H.B. 1627 § 20). Directs a dealer whose license is revoked or expires unrenewed to terminate all purchase, holding, and sale arrangements as prescribed by the director and send approved notices to creditors, sellers, and purchasers detailing resolution of open engagements. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Supervised operation during suspension and cost recovery
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 1980 H.B. 1627 § 20). Permits supervised operation during license suspension (including temporary suspension) and authorizes civil recovery from the dealer of administrative expenses, liability insurance, and daily fees computed under "subdivision (4) of subsection 1 of section 276.506" (retaining archived cross-reference; section 276.506(1) currently has only subdivisions (1)-(3) following 1997 H.B. 211). Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes. Verified archived cross-reference to "subdivision (4) of subsection 1 of section 276.506" against archived 276.506:14816, which contains only subdivisions (1)-(3) after 1997 H.B. 211; retained faithfully.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–2 and history note (L. 1980 H.B. 1627 § 20); verified all fingerprints. Confirmed termination/notice duties upon revocation or unrenewed expiration, supervised operation during suspension, circuit court recovery of expenses and liability insurance, and verified archived cross-reference in sub 2 to "subdivision (4) of subsection 1 of section 276.506" (absent in archived 276.506:14816, which ends at subdivision (3)). Retained both drafted titles and documented discrepancy explicitly.

headings.title: Petition for ex parte seizure and trustee possession
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/effective-date notes (L. 1980 H.B. 1627 § 21, A.L. 1986 H.B. 1578, A.L. 1997 H.B. 211; effective 4-02-97). Authorizes the director, upon evidence of dealer insolvency or inability to satisfy seller claims, to petition the principal-place-of-business circuit court for an ex parte order seizing and taking title and possession as trustee of grain, records, and property. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Scope and permissible terms of ex parte possession orders
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 including subdivisions (1)-(7) and history/effective-date notes. Authorizes circuit court ex parte possession orders (limited to grain-related assets where appropriate) including facility lock-downs, dealer/employee exclusion, transaction bans, freezing business and commingled personal accounts, grain redelivery/sale, court-controlled escrow, and document turnover. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Dealer response within ten days and fifteen-day hearing
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history/effective-date notes. Gives the dealer 10 days after possession to file a court response opposing retention, requires a hearing within 15 days of filing, and keeps the possession order unstayed until the court orders restoration after hearing. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Notice to bond surety and known grain sellers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history/effective-date notes. Requires the director upon taking possession to give written notice to the bond surety and permits notifying all known sellers shown in the dealer's records. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Duration of possession and nonoperation liability immunity
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history/effective-date notes. Directs retaining possession until seller claims are satisfied or court-ordered surrender, specifies no obligation to operate the dealer's business, and immunizes the director and agents from claims arising from nonoperation. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Petition for receiver to operate or liquidate business
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history/effective-date notes. Authorizes the director, whether or not in possession, to petition the circuit court for a receiver to operate or liquidate an insolvent dealer's business upon evidence of insolvency or inability to pay sellers. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Recovery of seizure and receivership expenses, fees, and insurance
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history/effective-date notes. Permits recovering necessary seizure and receivership expenses in a separate civil action or within the seizure/receivership proceeding, including a $100 per-person daily fee for facility seizure activities and necessary liability insurance costs. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–7 (including subdivisions (1)–(7) of sub 2) and history/effective-date notes (effective 4-02-97); verified all fingerprints. Confirmed ex parte insolvency seizure petitions, seven non-exhaustive order terms (including commingled personal accounts), 10-day response/15-day hearing without automatic stay, mandatory surety/permissive seller notice, nonoperation immunity, receivership petitions, and expense/$100-per-person-day/insurance recovery. All 7 drafted titles retained.

headings.title: Schedule of application, license, and special examination fees
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including subdivisions (1)-(3) and paragraphs (a)-(c), plus history/effective-date notes (L. 1980 H.B. 1627 § 22, A.L. 1997 H.B. 211; effective 4-02-97). Sets a $25 original filing fee, $40 original/renewal license fee, and special/requested/extra-work examination fees comprising section 33.090 personal expenses, section 33.095 mileage allowance, and $20 per man-hour. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes. Verified subdivisions (1)-(3) and paragraphs (a)-(c), confirming absence of the subdivision (4) cross-referenced in 276.496(2).

headings.title: Deposit of fees in general revenue without proration
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history/effective-date notes. Directs depositing all fees collected under sections 276.401 to 276.582 into the state general revenue fund and prohibits proration. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: License refusal, suspension, or revocation for unpaid fees
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history/effective-date notes. Makes nonpayment of fees grounds for refusing to issue or renew, or suspending or revoking, a grain dealer's license. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Filing and licensing fee exemption for chapter 411 licensees
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history/effective-date notes. Exempts grain dealers also licensed by Missouri under chapter 411 from application filing fees and licensing fees under sections 276.401 to 276.582. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Revised title to clarify the exemption covers application filing and licensing fees rather than special examination fees. (Prior draft: "Fee exemption for dual chapter 411 state licensees".)

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–4 (including subdivisions (1)–(3) and paragraphs (a)–(c) of sub 1) and history/effective-date notes (effective 4-02-97); verified all fingerprints. Confirmed $25 filing fee, $40 license fee, special examination rates citing sections 33.090 and 33.095, absence of any subdivision (4) referenced in 276.496(2), non-prorated general revenue deposit, unpaid-fee license sanctions, and dual chapter 411 exemption limited to application filing and licensing fees. Revised sub 4 title to avoid over-generalizing exemption; retained subs 1–3.

headings.title: Classification of dealers by business operation type
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/effective-date/footnote notes (L. 1980 H.B. 1627 § 23, A.L. 1986 H.B. 1578, A.L. 1997 H.B. 211; effective 4-02-97). Directs that all grain dealers be classified according to their type of business operation for regulatory purposes. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Class I dealer net worth and office-hours requirements
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 including subdivisions (1)-(3) and history/effective-date notes. Sets class I eligibility at net worth equal to the greater of $50,000 or 2% of grain purchases, requires six daily business hours between 8:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m. with posted hours (unless open 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.), and requires closure notices listing an accessible payment-authorized contact. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Class II licensed warehousemen and office-hours requirements
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 including subdivisions (1)-(2) and history/effective-date notes. Classifies chapter 411 or U.S. Warehouse Act warehousemen not meeting class I requirements as class II dealers and imposes the same daily business-hour, hours-posting, and closure-notice rules. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Class III bulk-facility dealers and office-hours requirements
